o.text:
From Proto-Common Turkic *kāš (“eyebrow; edge”), possibly from Proto-Turkic *kāĺ (“eyebrow; edge”). Cognate with Turkish kaş, etc.
The sense 'gemstone' might have developed from in the following way: 'eyebrow' → 'curved object' → 'ring frame' → 'gemstone', although it has sometimes also been seen as unrelated to the sense 'eyebrow'.

glosses: somewhere high; a place located at highs

o.text: From Arabic قَلْبِيّ (qalbi). By surface analysis, qəlb (“heart”) + -i (“-y; -al”)
From ev (“home, house”) + -lən. cognate with Turkmen öýlenmek and Chuvash авлан (avlan).
Borrowed from Russian ви́це-президе́нт (více-prezidént). By surface analysis, vitse- + prezident.
